# MLang Registry Protocol v1
This document specifies the first interoperable registry layout consumed by
`mlang pkg install`, `publish`, and `audit`. The protocol is intentionally
static-file friendly: a directory, object-storage bucket, CDN, and registry
service can expose the same read representation.

## Discovery and paths

The registry base URL or directory contains:

```text
config.toml
index/<normalized-package-name>.toml
packages/<normalized-package-name>/<version>/<archive>
advisories.toml
```

`config.toml` currently contains:

```toml
protocol = 1
```

Package names are normalized by replacing characters other than ASCII letters,
digits, `_`, and `-` with `_`. A client MUST still verify that the `name` in
the index matches the requested, unnormalized package name.

Local and `file://` registries use filesystem reads. HTTP registries serve the
same relative paths with GET. A successful response is the complete file;
redirects are allowed. Clients MUST reject transport errors and malformed or
unsupported index versions.

## Package index

`index/<name>.toml` has this schema:

```toml
protocol = 1
name = "hello"

[[version]]
version = "1.2.0"
archive = "packages/hello/1.2.0/hello-1.2.0.tar.gz"
checksum = "sha256:0123456789abcdef..."
signature = "packages/hello/1.2.0/hello-1.2.0.tar.gz.sig"
yanked = false
```

Required release fields are `version`, `archive`, and `checksum`. `version`
MUST be a complete semantic version and the checksum MUST identify SHA-256.
`signature` and `yanked` are optional. Unknown fields are reserved for
forward-compatible metadata and are ignored by v1 clients.

Resolution removes yanked versions, applies the requested semantic-version
range, and selects the greatest remaining version according to SemVer,
including prerelease ordering. A concrete cached version remains usable in
offline mode; yanking is not a substitute for a security advisory.

## Archives and verification

The v1 archive is gzip-compressed tar containing `mlang.toml` at its root.
Publishers SHOULD sort entries, normalize timestamps and ownership, and omit
the gzip timestamp so identical inputs produce identical archive bytes.
Clients MUST verify SHA-256 before extraction and MUST reject absolute paths or
any normalized path containing a `..` component. Publishers SHOULD reject
symbolic links; the reference `mlang pkg package` implementation does so.

If `signature` is present, clients MUST retrieve and verify it. The v1
signature profile is RSA/SHA-256 over the archive bytes, compatible with:

```sh
openssl dgst -sha256 -sign private.pem -out package.tar.gz.sig package.tar.gz
openssl dgst -sha256 -verify public.pem -signature package.tar.gz.sig package.tar.gz
```

Trust keys come from local client configuration or `--key`; they MUST NOT be
accepted from the package archive or an unauthenticated index. A policy may
require signatures even when the index does not declare one.

## Publishing API

Local publication copies immutable artifacts and atomically replaces the
package index. Remote publication sends:

```text
PUT <registry>/v1/packages/<normalized-name>/<version>
Authorization: Bearer <token>
Content-Type: multipart/form-data
```

Multipart fields:

| Field | Required | Meaning |
|---|---:|---|
| `archive` | yes | Package tarball bytes. |
| `checksum` | yes | `sha256:<hex>` of the archive. |
| `signature` | no | Detached signature bytes. |
| `signature_algorithm` | with signature | `rsa-sha256` in protocol v1. |

A registry service MUST authenticate publishers, enforce namespace ownership,
reject an already-published `(name, version)`, independently recompute the
checksum, validate metadata, store the release immutably, and serialize index
updates. Any 2xx response means publication succeeded; other statuses are
failures. The token is supplied through the environment variable named by
`[registry].token_env` so it does not appear in command logs.

## Advisory feed

`advisories.toml` uses:

```toml
protocol = 1

[[advisory]]
id = "MLANG-2026-0001"
package = "hello"
affected = ">=1.0.0, <1.2.3"
severity = "high"
title = "Example vulnerability"
url = "https://example.com/advisories/MLANG-2026-0001"
```

Required fields are `id`, `package`, and `affected`. Severity values understood
by the v1 client are `low`, `medium`/`moderate`, `high`, and `critical`.
Registries should retain advisories after a package is yanked because offline
lockfiles and mirrors may still contain the release.

## Caching and offline behavior

Indexes, archives, and signatures are cached below the global package cache in
a namespace derived from the registry location. Online resolution refreshes
the index. Offline resolution performs no HTTP request and requires cached
metadata and artifacts. Cached archive bytes are always rehashed, and cached
signatures are always reverified before installation.

See [Package Manager](Package-Manager#ecosystem-registry-packaging-install-audit-sbom-and-signing)
for user-facing commands and manifest configuration.
